title: The "shameful" measles data that lost the US its elimination status
gist: PAHO formally stripped the US of measles elimination status based on sustained transmission of a lineage beginning January 20, 2025 in Texas, using data only through January 2026, so this year's 5,400+ cases (including 1,500+ in Pennsylvania) and 10 deaths didn't factor in. With kindergarten MMR coverage at 92.4% and record exemptions, NSC chair Noel Brewer says the US problem is accelerating with no end in sight.

insights.claim: The US formally lost its measles elimination status, held since 2000, after PAHO's re-verification commission found sustained transmission of a single lineage for at least 12 months.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
insights.so_what: Endemic measles raises healthcare burden and public-health policy risk.

insights.claim: PAHO's decision used only data from January 2025 to January 2026, so the Pennsylvania outbreak that began in April did not contribute; the status was lost earlier and what is happening now is a runaway epidemic.
